compliance.emissions: FCC Class A, ICES-003 Issue 7, EN 55032:2015, VCCI-CISPR 32:2016, AS/NZS CISPR 32:2015

environmental.storage-temp-datasheet: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F), per the data sheet

features.encryption: none on the 7280CR3A-72; all ports (MACsec, IPsec and VXLANsec) on the 7280CR3AM-72 and 7280CR3AK-72
features.optics-qsfp28: each of the 72 QSFP cages runs 100G, or 40G (QSFP+), 50G and 25/10G modes by breakout (data sheet)
features.precision-timing: PTP and SyncE with OCXO and PPS/10M/ToD inputs

management.console: RJ-45 serial (RS-232), 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control

physical.size-over-ears: 48.3 x 8.8 x 68.7 cm (19 x 3.50 x 27.0 in) with the mounting ears (guide Table 1)
physical.weight: 22.4 kg (49.4 lbs) for the 7280CR3A-72, 7280CR3AM-72 and 7280CR3AK-72 (guide Table 1); 49.4 lbs (22.41 kg) in the data sheet

platform.software: EOS; minimum release 4.31.2 per the data sheet

power.power-draw-note: Data sheet: "406 W / 754 W", typical measured at 25 C ambient with 50 percent load on all ports, excluding transceivers. Guide Table 4 reads TBD.

thermal.airflow: front-to-rear or rear-to-front, set by the fan modules and supplies fitted

configs.name: ac1513-f

configs.description: Two PWR-1513-AC-BLUE supplies and rear-to-front air, with FAN-7012H-BLUE fan modules. Not an orderable build; see ac1513-f.
configs.name: ac1513-r

configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and four fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-1511-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7012H-RED fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKUs.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: Two DC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-1511-DC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7012H-BLUE fan modules. No DC part number is listed for the switch.
configs.name: dc-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3A-72 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-1512-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7012H-RED fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3A-72-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7280CR3AK-72 with large routes and TunnelSec, the same face, supplies and fans as the base switch, front-to-rear air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3AK-72-F.
configs.name: k-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3AK-72 with rear-to-front air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3AK-72-R.
configs.name: k-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3AM-72 with TunnelSec encryption, the same face, supplies and fans as the base switch, front-to-rear air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3AM-72-F.
configs.name: m-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3AM-72 with rear-to-front air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3AM-72-R.
configs.name: m-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3A-72 with two AC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-1512-AC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7012H-BLUE fan modules, all with blue handles. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3A-72-R.
configs.name: r

gaps.note: The 7280CR3AM-72 and 7280CR3AK-72 carry TunnelSec encryption on all ports, and the K build the large-routes licence, where the 7280CR3A-72 has neither. No configuration can state a device attribute (open gap #1237, accepted for now, decided 2026-10-23), so the device carries the base switch's features line and its encryption line names all three. The data sheet gives the builds one set of hardware figures.

The guide has no front figure for this model and the data sheet's photograph is 408 px wide (0.93 px/mm), so every front position is read to about a millimetre. Legends, lamp glyphs, the speed-strip print and the port numbers are not legible in it.
gaps.wanted: a flat figure or a studio photograph of the face.

gaps.note: The port numbers printed on the metal are not legible in the photograph and no held document lists them, so no numeral is printed and the port ids follow the library's other Arista boxes (provenance.port-numbering).
gaps.wanted: a photograph or figure of the numbered face.

gaps.note: The photograph is a picture of the K build and prints "7280CR3AK-72". The plain and M plates are not shown, so every configuration prints "7280CR3A-72".
The glyphs beside the four system lamps, the legends of the Time-of-Day slot and the two clock jacks, and the symbols at the management jacks are not legible and are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a flat figure or a photograph of the right-hand end of the face.

gaps.note: Neither the guide nor the data sheet names the clock connectors; they are seated as std/smb@1 from their drawn size and their direction (input or output) is not stated.
The Time-of-Day connector is seated as std/usb-c@1 because the data sheet's CAB-SYNCE-RJ names a USB-C mate.
Neither document gives the USB generation; the port is seated with the `usb2` skin as the one that claims least.
Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet). The guide's, the newer document, is in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The guide's Table 4 and section 4.4.1 name PWR-1511-AC as this model's supply; the data sheet's model comparison names PWR-1513-AC or PWR-1512-AC and its ordering information lists PWR-1512-AC-RED and -BLUE and PWR-1513-AC-RED and -BLUE. The data sheet's is used, because it is the one with orderable part numbers; both name PWR-1511-DC.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which AC supply ships.

gaps.note: The guide's chapter 3 figures are isometric drawings of other switches and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7201 and KIT-7004-2UL are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: The PWR-1511-DC supplies are the library's existing drawing of that module, an AC housing with a plain terminal block; the guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-1511-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.

gaps.wanted: a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

`attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port group qsfp28-100g - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 8.8 x 68.7 cm (19 x 3.50 x 27.0 in), 22.4 kg (49.4 lbs), the same for the 7280CR3A-72, 7280CR3AM-72 and 7280CR3AK-72. Data sheet: 43.99 x 8.79 x 68.69 cm "inc. handles" (17.3 x 3.46 x 27.04 in), 49.4 lbs (22.41 kg). The 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here); the height is the data sheet's 87.9 (the guide's 8.8 rounds it) and the depth its 686.9. 2RU.

colour.note: The front plate is #aaabad, the 7280CR3-32D4's reading of the same family's plate (the photograph's plate reads a similar light grey).

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280CR3A-72-F and -R, DCS-7280CR3AM-72-F and -R and DCS-7280CR3AK-72-F and -R, each "2 x AC", F for front to rear and R for rear to front air. The "#" orders ("configurable fans and psu") are orders of parts and are not listed. The A, M and K builds share the face, size, weight and supplies and differ in encryption and routes, which a configuration cannot state: see the gap config-scoped-device-attrs. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch (the PWR-1511-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares) and does not say which AC supply an -F or -R order carries, so the DC builds and the PWR-1513 builds are examples. No secure-boot (-S) build is listed for this family and the guide draws no blank for a bay, so no configuration shows an open bay.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's chapter 3 mounts the 2RU switch with the accessory-kit brackets in isometric drawings of other switches that carry no measure, and the kit guides are not held. The data sheet lists KIT-7201 and KIT-7004-2UL. No ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 90 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Only the storage temperature differs; the guide's, the newer document, is in attrs.

front-legend.note: A light plate at the upper left, 2.9 to 33.0 mm across and 3.1 to 12.0 mm down, carries the maker's wordmark and the model line. THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved. The model line is plain text and is set as "7280CR3A-72"; the photograph prints "7280CR3AK-72" because it is a picture of the K build, and the plain and M plates are not shown, so the same line is set on every configuration (gap model-plates).

front-ports.note: SEVENTY-TWO STACKED QSFP CAGES IN NINE BLOCKS, counted in a six-times enlargement of the photograph and confirmed by the data sheet ("72 x QSFP100"). A block is two columns of four rows (two stacked pairs of rows, a grey belly strip in each pair). The blocks' openings start at 14.0, 60.3, 106.7, 153.0, 200.4, 246.8, 293.1, 339.4 and 386.9 mm from the left (a 46.6 mm block pitch, 34 to 35 px wide each, a pair of 19.0 mm columns with an 8.6 mm gutter). The four rows' dark openings read 26.9 to 34.5, 42.0 to 50.6, 57.1 to 64.7 and 72.2 to 80.8 mm (a uniform 15.1 mm pitch), the 7280CR3A-48D6's grid, so the registry's 18.5 x 9.58 cage is seated with its top 0.5 mm above each opening. The belly-to-belly turn of each pair (upper cage upright, lower turned 180) is the library's convention; the photograph cannot show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E: "All fans and power supplies are hot swappable" and "all slots must be filled or covered with a blank for operation". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE FOUR FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit; the management ports are part of the chassis and are placements on the front. The held documents draw no blank for either bay, so none is modelled.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT IS DRAWN FROM THE DATA SHEET'S PHOTOGRAPH (page 6, "Arista 7280CR3A-72"), an embedded 408 x 248 px raster whose chassis fills 406 px across (x 1 to 406) and 82 px down (y 83 to 164). It is a near-straight-on render. Gate 1: 406 px across 440.0 mm gives 0.923 px/mm; 82 px down 87.9 mm gives 0.933 px/mm, one percent apart, so the face is near-orthographic and carries geometry. 0.928 px/mm is used on both axes, so one pixel is 1.08 mm and EVERY FRONT POSITION BELOW IS ESTIMATED to about 1 mm. The scale anchor is the 440.0 mm body (the data sheet's 43.99 cm over the handles) and its 87.9 mm height. The measure is a dark-run scan of the cage openings along x at the top rows and down the first column, read with a six-times enlargement beside it for the counts.

gate-1-rear.note: The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. This model has four fan modules, two supplies and is 2RU. Of the 2RU pair, D-3 has an earth grounding pad and D-4 none; the guide's Table 6 lists the 7280CR3A-72 as "Attach directly - right angle lug recommended" (the grounding location "is on the back for those supporting direct attach"), so it is mapped to figure D-3, as the 7280DR3A-36 and the 7280CR3-96 are, at the positions those files read off the same figure. THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED: it follows from fan count, height, supply count and Table 6, not from a caption.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-24 for an end-of-sale notice for the 7280CR3A-72, 7280CR3AM-72 and 7280CR3AK-72: none found for this family (the notices found are for older 7280 models), so the field reads none-announced.

management-ports.note: A row at the top right, in a frame 391.5 to 424.7 mm across and 4.8 to 22.3 mm down: the Ethernet management port at the left (with its two lamps at its left side), the USB port and the serial console at the right, centred at 400.1, 408.4 and 418.0 mm. Their spacing is closer than three upright jacks (15.8 mm wide each) allow, so the two RJ-45 jacks are TURNED A QUARTER (the Ethernet port 90, which puts its lamps at its left as the photograph shows them; the console 270) and the USB port stands on its end; the photograph's openings read 9.9 mm wide and 12.5 tall. Guide section 4.5: "For most models, the front panel contains the console, management, and USB ports"; the data sheet: "100/1000 Mgmt Ports 1", "USB Ports 1", "RS-232 Serial Ports 1 (RJ-45)". The management port is taken as 10/100/1000 (guide 4.5) and so 1g. Which of the two RJ-45 jacks is the console is read from the lamps, which only the Ethernet port has.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. Table 6 puts the 2RU grounding on the back for this model.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2 and Table 10: port LEDs sit near their ports (off link down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics). The photograph shows a green dot at the side of every row, left of the left column and right of the right column of each block, so each port carries one lamp beside it. Positions are read to a pixel.

port-numbering.note: THE PHOTOGRAPH'S PORT NUMBERS ARE NOT LEGIBLE AND NO DOCUMENT HELD LISTS THEM, so no numeral is printed. The ids follow the library's other Arista boxes: port-1 to port-72, the upper band of two rows first (1 to 36 from left to right) and the lower band after (37 to 72), the odd number the upper cage of each column as the 7280CR3-96's guide figure prints it. ESTIMATED; a photograph or figure of the numbered face closes it. EOS names ports Ethernet1 and up and Management1; they are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4 reads "TBD" for the power draw of all three builds. The data sheet gives 406 W typical and 754 W maximum (typical "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports, excludes transceivers"), used here. Supplies: Table 4 and section 4.4 name PWR-1511-AC and PWR-1511-DC; the data sheet's model comparison names "PWR-1513-AC, PWR-1512-AC or PWR-1511-DC" and its ordering information PWR-1512-AC-RED and -BLUE, PWR-1513-AC-RED and -BLUE and PWR-1511-DC-RED and -BLUE. The data sheet's PWR-1512-AC is the default (the library's reading for the same 1500 W housing), the PWR-1513-AC is accepted and shown in the examples, and the disagreement is recorded in the gap psu-part-numbers.

rear.note: Figure D-3 at the 7280DR3A-36 and 7280CR3-96 files' reading: four fan modules 79.6 mm wide and 81.5 mm tall at 5.9, 103.9, 189.4 and 274.9 mm across, a grounding strip 15.0 mm wide at 87.2 mm between the first and second fan with two ground screws and an earth symbol, and two supplies one above the other at 361.0 mm across (2.0 and 45.0 mm down, 73.5 mm wide, the data sheet's "73.5MM"). The guide's figure D-3 callout 7 names the "Earth grounding pad".

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7012H", spares FAN-7012H-RED (front-to-rear) and FAN-7012H-BLUE (rear-to-front). Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue one an air-inlet module. The four fan modules are bays that accept arista/7280dr3a-fan (FAN-7012H-RED) or arista/7050x4-fan-7012h-rev (FAN-7012H-BLUE), both reused by part number.

sources.note: 7280R3A Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, DOC-07042-01, 59 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3A.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage environment), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), Table 6 (grounding of the 2RU switches), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), section 4.5 (serial and management cables), Appendix A (status indicators, tables 9 to 13), Appendix D (rear panels, figures D-1 to D-4) and Appendix E (field replacement). The guide has NO FRONT FIGURE for this model: Appendix C draws only the DR3A-54 and DR3A-36. 7280R3A Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 04-0040-26, dated April 15th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3A-Datasheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280CR3A-72, 7280CR3AM-72 and 7280CR3AK-72, the power supply specifications, the ordering information and the platform overview, whose one photograph of this face is the only front source. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md, SOURCES.md (no 3D model, CAD drawing, studio photograph or Visio stencil is held; the stencil zip could not be fetched). No drawing or photograph is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: The photograph draws lavender strips above each block's two pairs of rows (the first at 24.0 mm down, the second at 53.6 mm), with print too small to read. They are drawn in that colour at the block width; the print is not drawn.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9: system status, fan status and a status lamp for each supply, four in a column at the right of the management row at 427.4 mm across and 8.4, 11.6, 15.0 and 18.6 mm down. The glyphs beside them are not legible, so no legend is drawn.

timing.note: At 6.7 mm down, left of the management row: two gold coax jacks at 350.0 and 359.2 mm across (about 4.8 mm) and a horizontal Time-of-Day slot with a screw at each end from 365.3 to 377.9 mm. The data sheet's "PTP and SyncE with OCXO and PPS/10M/ToD inputs" and its accessory "CAB-SYNCE-RJ  Spare Time of Day adapter cable (USB-C to 2 x RJ-45)" name the functions and a USB-C mate, so the slot is seated as std/usb-c@1 and the jacks as std/smb@1 (4.83 mm, which the photograph's size matches; an SMA is 6.35). The coax type is not stated. A green lamp beside the slot is not named by any document and is not drawn.

vents.note: The photograph fills the spaces not taken by a cage with a dotted vent grid: a deep band along the top (1.0 to 25.0 mm, with a lower part under the timing connectors), a band along the bottom, a column in each gutter between the blocks and one at each end. Each is drawn as one field in its measured extent, not hole by hole. A round hole at the left edge (7.0 mm across, 50.3 mm down) is drawn as a dark hole and carries no part; nothing names it.
